description: Overview Named after the elementary particle that binds quarks together inside atomic nuclei, QuantumGluon builds the optical hardware, quantum memory payloads, and orbital routing protocols required to extend the quantum internet beyond Earth's atmosphere. While terrestrial networks rely on fiber optics that lose quantum signals after a few hundred kilometers, QuantumGluon leverages the near-vacuum of space to distribute quantum entanglement across cislunar and deep-space distances.
summary:
QuantumGluon is an integrated space-based quantum networking architecture—paired with a Python orbital routing and link-budget simulation engine—that combines sub-microradian optical transceivers, cryogenic spin-wave quantum memory payloads, and asynchronous entanglement-swapping protocols.

Terrestrial silica fiber suffers exponential photon attenuation (~0.2 dB/km), limiting direct quantum communication to roughly 300 kilometers, while the no-cloning theorem prohibits classical signal amplification. QuantumGluon overcomes this barrier by operating in the near-vacuum of space, replacing exponential fiber absorption with manageable geometric diffraction. Our orbital nodes emit 1550 nm entangled photon pairs, buffer surviving qubits in rare-earth-doped memories with 1.2-second coherence lifetimes, and execute fidelity-optimized Bell measurements across LEO and cislunar L1/L2 halo constellations.

This architecture is critical for humanity’s expansion beyond Earth. By establishing a persistent cislunar quantum backbone, QuantumGluon enables physics-guaranteed quantum key distribution (QKD) for lunar infrastructure, networked orbital quantum processors, Earth-Moon baseline quantum telescopes, and sub-picosecond relativistic clock synchronization for deep-space navigation.
